headline: What a special district does
intro: A special district is a local government that state law sets up to do one job or a few, such as supplying water or fighting fires. It keeps enough control over its own work and money to count as a government of its own, apart from the county, city or town around it.
section: How the Census Bureau counts them
p1: The Census Bureau’s 2022 Census of Governments found 90,888 governments in the country: the federal government, the 50 states and 90,837 local governments. Special districts made up 39,555 of the local ones, more than four in ten.
p2: A district can go by many names, such as authority, board or commission. The state law that creates it names the jobs it may do, from running a library to building a transit line.
def_source: Source for the definition: U.S. Census Bureau, Census of Governments glossary, “Special district governments” and its function entries, United States. Retrieved November 21, 2026. The counts are the chart’s.
tagline: A country that answers to its people.
